title: Misliya Cave, Mount Carmel
summary: Prehistoric cave on Mount Carmel in northern Israel. A fossil upper jaw with teeth found there was dated by three methods to 177,000 to 194,000 years ago and identified as Homo sapiens, which would make it the earliest modern human fossil outside Africa; the age has been challenged.

uncertainty.note: Range of the three-method date for the Misliya-1 maxilla as published in 2018 (177,000 to 194,000 years).

where.modern_name: Misliya Cave, Mount Carmel, Haifa District, Israel
where.historical_name: Cave on the western slope of Mount Carmel in the Levant; no polities exist at this date

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Reconstruction to 0.185 Ma moves the point about 12 km; MULLER2019 gives 32.69 N, 34.92 E.

importance.justification: Candidate for the earliest Homo sapiens fossil outside Africa, pushing back dispersal estimates if the dates hold.
